primitives.name: Penalty Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: A side loses a certain distance, or the opponents may have a free kick, as a penalty for throttling, tripping up, or tackling below the knees.
primitives.assumptions: Penalty outcomes are deterministic functions of infractions within bounded spatial and temporal domains.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Infraction occurs below knee level with no intent to harm.

layer2.mapping: Maps player conduct to state-space displacement via probabilistic constraint enforcement.
layer2.telemetry: Ball position change, player movement vector deviation

primitives.name: Boundary Handling
primitives.verbatim_quote: When the ball goes out of bounds at the side, it is "put in" at the spot where it crossed the line by a player of the side first securing the ball.
primitives.assumptions: Ball exit is defined by crossing a fixed boundary with immediate re-entry control.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Ball crosses boundary line without clear possession.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to discrete event handling in control theory with boundary condition enforcement.
layer2.telemetry: Time of ball exit, player proximity to boundary

primitives.name: Officiating Hierarchy
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is the duty of the umpire to decide all points directly connected with the players' conduct, while the referee decides questions of the position or progress of the ball.
primitives.assumptions: Decision-making roles are mutually exclusive and temporally synchronized.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Conflicting decisions arise from overlapping jurisdiction.

layer2.mapping: Models decision authority as layered conditional probability distributions over game state.
